value.text: The S3 presign runner is the component keeping links fresh. I am now reading its implementation and the server startup wiring.

The component is the S3 presign runner (`s3presign.Runner`).

It refreshes presigned links every 12 hours. It is wired into server startup via `startBackgroundRunners` in `server/server.go`.

I have identified the component, its schedule, and its startup wiring.

The S3 presign runner (`s3presign.Runner` in `server/runner/s3presign`) refreshes links every 12 hours. It is wired into server startup at `server/server.go:129` via `s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)`, or created and started at `server/server.go:161-169`.

h01.
`s3presign.Runner` — every 12 hours — `server/server.go:129`

The runner in `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go` re-presigns S3 attachment URLs so they do not expire (it skips objects still valid for the next 4 days). `runnerInterval` is `12 * time.Hour`. `Server.Start` wires it in by calling `startBackgroundRunners`, which constructs the runner, runs it once immediately, then starts `Run` in a background goroutine.

value.text:
I am analyzing the repository to locate the outbound HTTP notification delivery function and its protection against internal network addresses.

The outbound delivery executes in `webhook.Post` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. `PostAsync` merely queues to workers that call `Post`.

`safeDialContext` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` prevents DNS rebinding during dial. `ValidateURL` and `isReservedIP` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` reject reserved and private IP ranges when creating or updating webhooks.

I am weighing whether to pair the delivery function with `safeDialContext` or with `ValidateURL`, since both mechanisms block internal address targeting.

I have settled on `Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`; `safeDialContext` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. `safeDialContext` blocks the actual HTTP client from dialing internal addresses during delivery, while `ValidateURL` only rejects them at registration time.

h02.
`webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`; `safeDialContext` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`

Outbound webhook POSTs run in `Post` via `safeClient`. That client’s `DialContext` is `safeDialContext`, which resolves the host and refuses reserved/private IPs (loopback, RFC-1918, link-local/IMDS, and IPv6 equivalents in `internal/webhook/validate.go`) so delivery cannot be aimed at the internal network, including after DNS rebinding. `ValidateURL` applies the same reserved-IP check when a webhook URL is stored.

value.text:
The avatar request chain begins at `serveUserAvatar` in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`. `GetUserAvatar` is only a leftover ACL entry with no RPC in the proto. The browser path is fileserver.

`getUserByUsername` in `fileserver.go` calls `Store.GetUser` in `store/user.go`, then `Store.ListUsers` there because username lookup bypasses the ID cache. `Driver.ListUsers` in `store/driver.go` is the interface. `DB.ListUsers` in `store/db/sqlite/user.go` and its MySQL/PostgreSQL equivalents are the concrete data layer hops. `parseDataURI` runs after data retrieval, so it is not a data-layer hop. `RegisterRoutes` wires the handler.

The avatar data lives in `user.avatar_url` as a data URI, returned inside the user row.

h07.
`serveUserAvatar` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`  
`getUserByUsername` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`  
`Store.GetUser` — `store/user.go`  
`Store.ListUsers` — `store/user.go`  
`Driver.ListUsers` — `store/driver.go`  
`DB.ListUsers` — `store/db/sqlite/user.go` (same method in `store/db/mysql/user.go`, `store/db/postgres/user.go`)

The browser hits `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`. The handler loads that user by username; `GetUser` does not cache username lookups, so it goes through `ListUsers` to the driver, which reads `avatar_url` from the `user` table. The image bytes themselves are the data-URI stored in that column, decoded in `parseDataURI` in the same fileserver file. There is no `GetUserAvatar` RPC in `proto/api/v1/user_service.proto` (only a leftover ACL entry).

value.description: List all Go files under internal/

value.text:
A Python script will parse internal/*.go files and count inbound callers across the repository to identify the function with the highest fan-in.

The script will disambiguate colliding names by tracking package, type, and name. Unique names are simpler to count, but shared names like New or String require careful handling. Methods will be counted as Type.Method to distinguish same-name methods on different types.

args.command:
python3 << 'PY'
import os, re
from collections import defaultdict

root = "/bench/repo"
internal = os.path.join(root, "internal")

# Match function/method declarations
decl_re = re.compile(
    r'^func\s+(?:\((?P<recv>[^)]+)\)\s+)?(?P<name>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*\('
)

# Collect declarations from non-test internal files? Question says declared under internal/
# I'll include both test and non-test declarations, but prefer non-test for "the" function.
decls = []  # (pkg_path, type_or_None, name, file, line, is_test)

for dirpath, _, files in os.walk(internal):
    for f in files:
        if not f.endswith('.go'):
            continue
        path = os.path.join(dirpath, f)
        rel = os.path.relpath(path, root)
        is_test = f.endswith('_test.go')
        with open(path) as fh:
            for i, line in enumerate(fh, 1):
                m = decl_re.match(line)
                if not m:
                    continue
                name = m.group('name')
                recv = m.group('recv')
                typ = None
                if recv:
                    # recv like "s *Service" or "c Cache"
                    parts = recv.split()
                    typ = parts[-1].lstrip('*')
                decls.append((rel, typ, name, i, is_test, line.strip()))

print(f"Total declarations: {len(decls)}")
print(f"Non-test: {sum(1 for d in decls if not d[4])}")

# Unique symbols
from collections import Counter
names = Counter()
for rel, typ, name, i, is_test, line in decls:
    key = f"{typ}.{name}" if typ else name
    names[key] += 1

print("\nMost common declaration names (possible overloads):")
for k,v in names.most_common(20):
    print(f"  {v:3} {k}")
PY

The initial search results are polluted by common identifiers. `New` appears 325 times because it is a frequent constructor name, and `SortVersion.Len` appears 317 times because `Len(` is extremely common. These false positives obscure the true internal/ fan-in counts.

`Next(` and `CompileToStatement(` are additional common-name false positives. A precise count must distinguish package-level functions from methods, filter out stdlib collisions, and tally per distinct declaration rather than per name.

GenUUID with 28 callers, CompileToStatement with 38, and NewEngine with 32 appear to be genuine high-fan-in declarations. The next step is to verify these candidates and check utility functions for similarly high inbound counts.

Test files likely inflate call counts, so the revised analysis will exclude non-test declarations and focus on production-only callers. A cleaner script will isolate unique internal/ symbols and count their exact inbound callers.

Symbols declared outside internal/ will be skipped to avoid false positives. Exact patterns `.Name(` for methods and `Name(` for functions will be used. The top unique declarations will be listed with sample call sites. Convert* helpers and resource name utilities are also being checked.

value.text:
CompileToStatement, NewEngine, and NewSchema likely inflate fan-in counts due to test call sites. Careful counting is needed to identify the true highest inbound caller.

A perl script will distinguish call sites from unique callers and separate production from test usage. addArg may show high self-fan-in from repeated calls within one file. CompileToStatement has roughly 30 test sites plus production and declaration calls.

Other candidates include Field, jsonArrayExpr, renderChildren, markdown Service methods, and filter helpers such as isReservedIP. GenUUID shows roughly 27 inbound call sites. Precise counts are now being tallied.

value.text:
Only one concrete implementation exists: the unexported `markdown.service`, created by `markdown.NewService`.

`NewAPIV1Service` in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go` creates the service with tag and mention extensions. It passes the result to `rss.NewRSSService` in `server/server.go`. `APIV1Service` and `RSSService` both hold the interface. `memopayload.Runner` also stores it, though it is never instantiated in production; only `RebuildMemoPayload` uses the service directly.

h13.
`markdown.service` — `markdown.NewService` in `NewAPIV1Service` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go`); holders: `APIV1Service` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go`), `RSSService` (`server/router/rss/rss.go`; same instance from `server/server.go`), and `memopayload.Runner` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`, unused at runtime)

The `markdown.Service` interface is implemented only by the unexported `service` in `internal/markdown/markdown.go`. Production builds it once with `WithTagExtension` and `WithMentionExtension`, stores it on `APIV1Service`, and hands that same value to RSS. Memo create/update call `RebuildMemoPayload` with `s.MarkdownService`; they do not construct a second impl.

value.text:
Derived metadata is stored in MemoPayload, combining tags and property flags. It is computed by RebuildMemoPayload via markdown.ExtractAll. CreateMemo always triggers recomputation.

UpdateMemo triggers recomputation when the content path changes. Mentions are extracted but not persisted in the payload. A background runner rebuilds all memos, though it is never called in production.

value.text:
The computation site is `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` in `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`, which calls `markdown.Service.ExtractAll`. It triggers on `CreateMemo` and `CreateMemoComment`.

It also triggers on `UpdateMemo` when the content is in the update mask. `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` rebuilds all payloads but is never invoked in production. It extracts tags, link presence, code presence, task list presence, incomplete task presence, and the first H1 title. Mentions are collected but not persisted. These values feed list previews.

h14.
`memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`) via `markdown.Service.ExtractAll` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go`); `CreateMemo` always and `UpdateMemo` when `content` is in the update mask (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`; comments go through `CreateMemo`); tags (`#tag`) plus `MemoPayload.Property`: `has_link`, `has_code`, `has_task_list`, `has_incomplete_tasks`, and `title` (first H1)

`ExtractAll` also collects `@mentions`, but `RebuildMemoPayload` only writes `Tags` and `Property` onto `storepb.MemoPayload` (`proto/store/memo.proto`). Location is user-set, not derived. `Runner.RunOnce` would rebuild every memo but is not wired into production.

value.description: Find cron scheduler jobs and DB cleanup

value.text:
There is no nightly database-cleanup job. The scheduler package contains a "daily-cleanup" example in doc.go, but it is never used or registered in production.

The s3presign runner runs every 12 hours via ticker, not cron.

r03.
There is no nightly database-cleanup cron job. `internal/scheduler` is a reusable cron library with a `"daily-cleanup"` example in `internal/scheduler/doc.go`; nothing in `cmd/` or `server/` constructs a scheduler or registers jobs. The only background runner is S3 URL re-presign on a 12-hour ticker (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go`, started from `server/server.go`). Cache expiry cleanup is in-process every 5 minutes (`store/cache/cache.go`), not a DB job.

r04.
